flags: Host L.P. amended and restated its senior unsecured bank credit facility. The restatement refinanced the revolver and two term loan tranches and extended the revolver maturity, with a new leverage-based pricing adjustment.
The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for comparable hotel RevPAR growth and Total RevPAR growth, both above the high end of its prior ranges.
The company entered into a new at-the-market common stock distribution agreement for up to $600 million of shares. It replaces the prior agreement, which still had the same amount unsold.
no_value_reason: no valuation route for this kind of company yet (real estate, pre-profit biotech)

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: Host Hotels & Resorts owns hotels and earns its money from them. It describes itself as the largest publicly traded lodging REIT, with a portfolio of luxury and upper-upscale hotels. The consolidated portfolio is 76 hotels with approximately 41,700 rooms, almost all in the U.S.
quotes: We are the largest publicly traded lodging REIT, with a geographically diverse portfolio of luxury and upper-upscale hotels.

business_model.claim: Host does not operate its hotels. Third-party managers run them under long-term agreements and earn fees tied to hotel revenue and profit. Host funds working capital and receives a monthly cash distribution of hotel-level sales less property-level operating expenses (excluding depreciation).
quotes: Our hotels are operated by third-party managers under long-term agreements, pursuant to which they typically earn base and incentive management fees based on the levels of revenues and profitability of each hotel.
We generally receive a cash distribution from our hotel managers each month, which distribution reflects hotel-level sales less property-level operating expenses (excluding depreciation).

business_model.claim: Marriott is the dominant operating partner. Approximately 64% of Host's hotels, measured by 2025 hotel revenues, are managed or franchised by Marriott International, so Host depends on one counterparty for most of its revenue.
quotes: Approximately 64% of our hotels (as measured by 2025 hotel revenues) are managed or franchised by Marriott International.

business_model.basis: Mix percentages stated in 10-K Item 7. The business and high-end leisure target is stated in the risk factors.
business_model.claim: Customers fall into three groups: transient, group and contract business. They accounted for approximately 61%, 34% and 5% of 2025 room sales. Hotels target business and high-end leisure travelers.
quotes: Our customers fall into three broad groups: transient business, group business and contract business, which accounted for approximately 61%, 34%, and 5%, respectively, of our 2025 room sales.

business_model.basis: Percentages are stated in the 10-K. Dollar figures are taken from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Hotel revenues were about 98% of 2025 total revenues, and condominium sales were the remaining 2%. Within hotel revenues, rooms were 60%, food and beverage 30% and other ancillary 10%. For the nine months ended September 30, total revenues of 4,632 (table in millions) were rooms 2,738, food and beverage 1,368, other 440 and condominium sales 86.
quotes: Hotel revenues represented approximately 98% of our total 2025 revenues, while the remaining 2% related to condominium sales.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 7 and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Room revenue is driven by occupancy and average daily rate, which multiply to RevPAR. In the third quarter, comparable hotel RevPAR was $219.50, up 8.8%, with rate increases of 5.7% and occupancy up 2.1 points.
quotes: RevPAR is defined as the product of the average daily room rate charged and the average daily occupancy achieved.
Comparable hotel RevPAR was $219.50, an increase of 8.8% compared to the same period in 2025, reflecting rate increases of 5.7% and an increase in occupancy of 2.1 points.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The 1.2% appears in the MD&A table.
business_model.claim: Reported revenue growth in the third quarter was much smaller than RevPAR growth. Total revenues rose only 1.2% against comparable RevPAR growth of 8.8%, because dispositions removed $80 million of revenue in the quarter.
quotes: the reduction of $80 million in revenues in the third quarter

business_model.basis: Figures are from the 10-Q income statement. The wage share is stated in the 10-K.
business_model.claim: Costs are mostly hotel-level expenses. For the nine months, total operating costs and expenses were 3,899 (table in millions), including rooms 680, food and beverage 911, other departmental and support 1,099 and management fees 197. Wages and benefits are a large part, about 58% of the rooms, food and beverage and other departmental and support expenses.
quotes: Taken separately, these costs represent approximately 58% of our rooms, food and beverage, and other departmental and support expenses.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 7. The 10-K risk factor 'Our expenses may not decrease if our revenues decrease' supports this.
business_model.claim: Some costs are relatively fixed. Property taxes, ground rent, equipment rent and insurance do not necessarily fall when revenue falls, and debt service and wages are also inflexible. This gives the business operating leverage, so a revenue decline hits profit hard.
quotes: Many of these expenses are relatively inflexible and do not necessarily change based on changes in revenues at our hotels.

business_model.basis: Figures are from the 10-Q statements. The strategy is stated in the 10-K.
business_model.claim: Host recycles capital by selling and buying hotels, which produces non-operating gains. Other gains were 235 (table in millions) in the nine months, inside net income of 813 (table in millions). Proceeds from asset sales were 1,078 (table in millions).
quotes: Similarly, we intend to continue our capital recycling program with strategic and opportunistic dispositions.

business_model.basis: Figures are from the 10-Q cash flow statement. The need is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
business_model.claim: Hotels need continuing reinvestment. Renewals and replacements cost 218 (table in millions) and return-on-investment projects 174 (table in millions) in capital expenditures for the nine months. The 10-K says hotels need capital spending to stay competitive and meet management agreements.
quotes: We need to make capital expenditures to remain competitive with other hotels, to maintain the economic value of our hotels and to comply with applicable laws and regulations.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors, the balance sheet and the 8-K.
business_model.claim: As a REIT, Host must pay out at least 90% of taxable income as dividends and relies on external capital to grow. It carries total debt of 5,084 (table in millions) and, after the quarter, set up an at-the-market stock program of up to $600 million.
quotes: Since we have elected REIT status, Host Inc. must finance its growth and fund debt repayments largely with external sources of capital because it is required to pay dividends to its stockholders in an amount equal to at least 90% of its taxable income (other than net capital gain) each year to qualify as a REIT.
having a combined aggregate offering price of up to $600 million

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors. The customer-demand view is stated in the 10-K outlook.
business_model.claim: Revenue is cyclical and tied to the economy. The 10-K says lodging demand typically follows the general economy, so results can swing widely. Management expects the high-income customers who make up most of its guests to keep travelling.
quotes: Because lodging industry demand typically follows the general economy, the lodging industry is highly cyclical, which contributes to potentially large fluctuations in our financial condition and our results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 text; the effect of scale on results is inferred.
competitive_position.claim: Host describes itself as the largest publicly traded lodging REIT. Its consolidated portfolio is 76 mainly luxury and upper-upscale hotels with about 41,700 rooms, nearly all in the U.S. Scale is its stated base for a data-driven asset-management platform.
quotes: We are the largest publicly traded lodging REIT, with a geographically diverse portfolio of luxury and upper-upscale hotels.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Operating momentum in Q3 2026 was strong. Comparable hotel RevPAR rose 8.8% and Total RevPAR rose 7.3%, with room rates up 5.7% and occupancy up 2.1 points. Management raised full-year guidance to 6.75% RevPAR growth and 6.0% Total RevPAR growth.
quotes: Delivered Comparable Hotel RevPAR Growth of 8.8% and Comparable Hotel Total RevPAR Growth of 7.3%
Raising Full Year 2026 Growth Guidance for Comparable Hotel RevPAR to 6.75% and Total RevPAR to 6.0%
reflecting rate increases of 5.7% and an increase in occupancy of 2.1 points.

competitive_position.basis: Inferred from the line items in the income statement; the statement does not name the cause.
competitive_position.claim: Q3 operating profit rose while net income fell. Operating profit was 121 against 101, but net income was 71 against 163 (table in millions). Other gains swung from 122 to (6), which explains much of the net income drop.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as management guidance, so it is a forward-looking expectation.
competitive_position.claim: Management expects rate gains to cover wage inflation, which is evidence of pricing power in the luxury and upper-upscale tier. It guides full-year operating profit margin and comparable hotel EBITDA margin higher than in 2025.
quotes: Full year operating profit margins and comparable hotel EBITDA margins are expected to increase compared to 2025, as rate improvements offset increases in wage expense.

competitive_position.basis: Debt and cash figures are from the balance sheet. The credit facility terms are stated in the 8-K and release. The investment-grade goal is stated in the 10-K; the evidence does not give the current rating.
competitive_position.claim: Host keeps an investment-grade balance sheet as a stated competitive pillar. Total debt was 5,084 at Sep 30, 2026 against 5,077 at year-end 2025, with cash of 1,492 (table in millions). The credit facility was amended in October 2026 and the revolver now matures January 15, 2031.
quotes: Our goal is to maintain a flexible capital structure that allows us to execute our strategy throughout the lodging cycle.
Amended $2.5 Billion Credit Facility, Extending Maturity and Improving Pricing Grid

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the filings; the strategic purpose is stated by management.
competitive_position.claim: Host is recycling capital by selling hotels and buying new ones. Nine-month asset-sale proceeds were 1,078 against 121 a year earlier (table in millions). Subsequent to the 2025 year-end it sold two Four Seasons resorts for $1.1 billion. It has also bought 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge and Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West.
quotes: Subsequent to year-end, we sold the Four Seasons Resort Orlando at Walt Disney World® Resort and the Four Seasons Resort and Residences Jackson Hole for a sales price of $1.1 billion.
Acquired 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge and Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West Hotel

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement; the link to sale proceeds is inferred.
competitive_position.claim: Nine-month shareholder payouts were much larger than a year earlier. Dividends on common stock were 1,007 against 486, and stock repurchases were 75 against 205 (table in millions). Operating cash flow was 1,190 against 967.

Host is investing in transformational renovations with Hyatt and Marriott, who contribute priority returns and operating profit guarantees. This is meant to keep hotels competitive in their markets and to offset disruption.
quotes: Hyatt has agreed to provide additional priority returns on the agreed upon investments and operating profit guarantees totaling $40 million to offset expected business disruptions.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: Concentration in one operator. About 64% of hotels by 2025 hotel revenue are managed or franchised by Marriott International. Host does not run its hotels, so adverse developments at Marriott could hurt it.
quotes: Approximately 64% of our hotels (as measured by 2025 hotel revenues) are managed or franchised by Marriott International.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: Cyclicality and exposure to the luxury and business-travel segments. The majority of hotels are luxury or upper upscale and target business and high-end leisure travelers, so revenue may fall more in a downturn.
quotes: Consequently, our hotels may be more susceptible to a decrease in revenues during an economic downturn, as compared to hotels in other categories that have lower room rates.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: Competition from other hotel owners and chains, and from online channels, including generative AI search, which could raise distribution costs. Host also competes for acquisitions.
quotes: The lodging industry is highly competitive.
Search engines (including generative AI search) and peer-to-peer inventory sources also provide online travel services that compete with our hotels.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: Debt and its covenants. Total debt was about $5.1 billion at December 31, 2025. The 10-K says it requires a significant portion of annual operating cash flow for debt service and that covenants restrict acquisitions and dividends without certain leverage metrics.
quotes: We have significant indebtedness and may incur additional indebtedness.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 8-K; the purpose of the program is not stated in the shown text.
competitive_position.claim: Host replaced its at-the-market equity program with a new one for up to $600 million of common stock. This is an optional source of capital, and the company is not obligated to sell shares.
quotes: The Company is not obligated to sell, and none of the Sales Agents are obligated to buy or sell, any Shares under the Distribution Agreement.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 10-K risk factors.

In Q3 2026 an active Hawaii hurricane season and a one-month closure of Alila Ventana Big Sur for wildfire evacuations weighed on results. The 10-K lists wildfires and hurricanes as risks to occupancy.
quotes: and further reduced by the one-month closure of Alila Ventana Big Sur due to wildfire evacuations.
